label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, secret-rotation, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 11 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy webhook-receiver: WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION v2 -> v1); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: secret-rotation
case.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff.
case.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

expected_symptoms: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, the provider's webhooks not acknowledged, and the books rule fires at its second evaluation, about 50 s after the deploy
the receiver refuses every webhook with a 400, counts it as bad_signature and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'; the provider sends its growing backlog again and again, tens of times a second
nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka

payments and refunds still go through, but one whose answer was lost cannot be confirmed: its client's retries get 503 again, so the 5xx share of POST /payments about doubles and its p95 climbs to about 0.6 s, both under their thresholds

after the rollback the books catch up within about three minutes: the provider sends each refused webhook again within a minute of its last try, and one whose acknowledgement is then lost (the traffic's noise) a minute later
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, 190 of the provider's webhooks up to it had not been acknowledged yet.

diagnosis.hypothesis: webhook-receiver was recreated at 19:22:12Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. Within seconds, every incoming webhook began failing its signature check (result=bad_signature), and 'queued' results stopped. No events reach provider-events, and no webhook is acknowledged. The provider keeps redelivering, and new charges and refunds add to the pile. Intake climbed from about 3/s to about 27/s, and the unacknowledged count grew from 190 at the alert to 261. The money check therefore cannot settle up to its cutoff. The most likely explanation is that the provider still signs with the previous secret and the receiver now checks against v2. A wrong or missing v2 secret on the receiver would look the same. Either way, the redeploy is the trigger.

evidence.shows: A fresh money check, waiting 30 s, could not run: 261 webhooks were not acknowledged by our receiver. That is up from 190 at the alert, so the backlog is growing.
webhook-receiver is the only service changed since 19:20:46Z. It was redeployed at 19:22:12Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. fake-provider shows no settings and no change since 19:20:46Z.

'bad_signature' first appears at 19:22:25, 13 s after the deploy, and climbs to about 27/s. 'queued' is last seen at 19:22:40, which fits a 1m rate window draining after the switch. Since then, every webhook is rejected.

The total receive rate rose from about 0.5/s to about 27/s after the deploy. That fits redeliveries of unacknowledged webhooks piling up. Its grouping labels do not exist (see c6), so it shows only the total.
klaxon_webhooks_received_total has a 'result' label, which is what c7 splits by. c5's labels are not on this metric.
All services are running and healthy with no restarts. Only webhook-receiver started later, at 19:22:12Z. Kafka, the consumers, postgres and redis show no fault.
The receiver logged no WARN or ERROR lines in the last 10 minutes, despite rejecting everything. The rejections are invisible at those log levels, which is an observability gap.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to the settings it ran before the 19:22:12Z deploy, so it verifies with the secret the provider signs with. Then confirm that klaxon_webhooks_received_total{result="queued"} resumes and bad_signature drops to near zero. Re-run the money check to confirm the backlog drains through provider redeliveries. Any move to v2 must be coordinated with the provider's signing secret first. Separately, log signature rejections at WARN or above.

diagnosis.blast_radius: webhook-receiver pauses while its container is recreated, so a few more deliveries fail briefly; the provider retries them. Once accepted, the backlog of roughly 260+ redeliveries arrives in a burst onto provider-events. ledger-consumer runs LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and payment-confirmer runs by_our_id, so duplicate redeliveries should not double-book, though the burst may briefly raise consumer lag. If the provider in fact moved to v2, the rollback would keep rejecting webhooks, and nothing would get worse than now. No money was booked wrong: rejected events were never processed.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If bad_signature persists or rises after the rollback, the provider may be signing with v2. Redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2 after verifying that the v2 secret value matches the provider's. Webhooks that remain unacknowledged keep being redelivered by the provider, so neither state loses events.
